findings.claim: The loop-2 hardening of test_task01 (test_main.py:163-168) now rejects any ListComp, SetComp or DictComp anywhere in read_csv or read_jsonl as 'not streaming'. That is a wrongly failing check with a false message. A per-record comprehension still streams one record at a time. Probe dictcomp_row in scratch: read_csv yielding `{key: value for key, value in row.items()}` inside the DictReader loop, with every result unchanged, fails with 'Task 1: read_csv must stream record by record, not read the whole file first'. The same applies to a per-row key or value cleanup such as `{k.strip(): v for ...}`, which a learner may add while looking at the messy CSV fixture. The README dictates `yield row`, so few learners will hit it; when one does, the message is false and blocks them.
findings.recommendation: Flag a comprehension only when it collects records rather than transforming one record: for example, when its generator iterates the file object or the DictReader (comp.generators[0].iter is the name bound by the with statement, or a DictReader/open call), or when it is not inside a yield. Alternatively, drop the comprehension rule and rely on the existing read/readlines/list/sorted/tuple and Starred checks, plus the generator behaviour already asserted.
